page.layout: One page of running text, with two right-margin notes ("Lect.4" beside the verse quotation and "9.Maij" beside its second line). Above the text, the running head "COMMENTARIA." with page number 143 at top right. Below the last line, the catchword "Im-" at right.

main_text.p: expellunt lutum & cœnum. Nulla est pax, inquit Deus meus, improbis. Isa.57.24.25.
main_text.head: QVAENAM DOCTRINAE CAPITA ex hoc loco colligis?
main_text.p: 1. Improbos pyraustę gaudium gaudere, eoq; nomine minimè formidandos nobis esse.
2 Cauendum pijs ab impostura sophistica, quæ facit temporariam profperitatem impiorū, opinetur pacis nomine digna esse.
main_text.head: VERSVS IIII. ET V.

p.i: Quia non sunt constructiones ad mortemLect.4. ipsorum: & firmum est robur eorum. In mo-9.Maij. lestijs non sunt, & cum hominibus non flagellantur.

main_text.p: Propheta instituit Inductionem, cuius ordo duplex est. Primò enim persequitur quasdam causas, v.4.5 deinde, effectus internos & externos exponit, v.6.,8.9. postremò, Apostatarum fata describit, mentionem facta defectionis filiorum Dei ad filios huius seculi, v.10. 11,12.
main_text.head: INDVCTIO PRIMA DE CAVSSIS.
main_text.p: Improbi homines, nō laborant constri-ctione ad mortem ipsorum, hoc est, fruuntur prosperâ valetudine, sic ut extra morborum & propemodum mortis aleam positi videantur. Econtrà pij sæpenumerò conflictan-tur morbis, & ut videtur, morte immatura decedunt. Im-

page.notes: Isa.57.24.25 and the verse numbers in the cross-references are copied as printed and may differ from the Vulgate numbering; please check. The marginal notes "Lect.4." and "9.Maij." are read from the scan and are uncertain. "pyraustę" is read as printed; the long s in "sophistica" and "esse" is transcribed as s. The catchword "Im-" is taken from the foot of the page.
